independent_anchors.source_description: Book ch05 (KB ch05_exchange_money_price.md L1591-1593): 'In the seventy-six years from 1933 to 2009, the dollar price of gold rose almost forty-seven-fold (4,568%)'. The 'from 1933' base is the official pre-devaluation gold price ($20.67/oz = index 100, the 1929-1932 plateau that officially held through 1933 until FDR's Jan-1934 devaluation); den_year=1932 is the last unambiguous official-price year. Pipeline 2009/1932 = 47.17x reproduces the ~47-fold claim. NOTE (F-P2.1-02): Shaikh's own USGoldpriceindex 1933 annual-average value (118.24) legitimately reflects the late-1933 RFC gold-buying run-up and is faithfully reproduced; measuring the fold-rise from that run-up-inclusive 1933 value (39.9x) is NOT what the book's 47-fold prose asserts.

S903.display_name: Actual wage-profit curves for the US economy, 1947-1998

triage.reason: Faithful reconstruction of Shaikh's actual (empirical) wage-profit curves, Figures 9.8, 9.12 and 9.19 (Ch9, Section X). For each US benchmark year the fixed-capital price system is solved for the wage share at each rate of profit (WSHARE), then rescaled by a Penn World Tables productivity index (PWT 7.1) into a real-wage curve (WRCURVE) plotted over its own profit-rate range up to that year's maximum profit rate (R). Construction-relevant: the empirical near-linear wage-profit curves that underpin Shaikh's transformation-problem and choice-of-technique arguments. Subseries carry genuinely different meanings and units (wage share, real-wage productivity index, productivity index, maximum profit rate), so units are split per subseries. NOTE: Figure 9.19's printed caption reads '1947-1972' and plots curves wr47-wr72 only, while the narrative (p.422) and this dataset cover 1947-1998; the display_name follows the data and text. SPARSE flag on S903-R-CIRC is a non-issue: it is a single scalar (one circulating-capital maximum profit rate), correctly one row.

S1406.notes: HARD GATE: productivity formula implemented literally; loader emits assertion failure if any per-hour FRED ID is added to FRED_INPUTS. | 2026-07-01 DF-1 REMEDIATED (SWEEP-ch1417-01): the 2012+ productivity denominator was FRED B4701C0A222NBEA, which is 'Hours worked by full-time and part-time employees' (BEA NIPA T6.9, millions of hours), NOT full-time-equivalent EMPLOYEES. Shaikh Appendix 14.2 p.892 requires FEE = full-time equivalent employment (NIPA T6.5A-D). Feeding hours into yr=(GDP*100/p)/(FEE/1000) made the extension output-per-HOUR growth mislabeled per-FTE, silently defeating the per-hour concept guard. Replaced with FRED A4301C0A173NBEA ('Full-time equivalent employees', total, NIPA T6.5A-D, thousands); broadened assert_no_per_hour_substitution to also reject hours-worked denominators (B4701C0*). Book rows (<=2011) byte-identical; S1406-B extension 2012+ recomputed (splice 2011->2012 GREEN); S1406-A (inflation) unaffected. Extension now reaches 2024 (was 2022) since the FTE series is current through 2024.

XS003.display_name: Imputed-interest adjustment and corrected sectoral profit rates

triage.reason: HEADLINE MIXED-UNITS FIX. Series interleaves two genuinely different quantities: three dollar imputed-interest adjustments (A-C, billions, can be negative) and four decimal profit rates (D-G, ~0.03-0.19). Under the banned series-level 'mixed_billions_usd_and_decimal_rates' string it rendered as one nonsensical spiky line (the canonical AS003/XS003 failure in UNITS_VALIDATION_STANDARD) and fails gate P14. After per-subseries units the A-C dollar panel and the D-G rate panel each render sensibly one-trace-per-subseries. These corrected profit rates are the empirical objects feeding S601-S604 and Ch16 dynamics.

provenance.shaikh_source: Shaikh (2020) 'An Empirically Sufficient Form for Sraffa Prices' Tables 1-2 (solo)
provenance.shaikh_appendix_ref: Shaikh (2020 working paper; publ. as Shaikh (2024), 'An Empirically Sufficient Form for Sraffa Prices', Structural Change and Economic Dynamics 69:1-9, ScienceDirect PII S0954349X23001480); Tables 1-2, eqs 6, 8, 10
provenance.conceptual_continuity: Same Sraffa aggregate price-value ratio computation (paper eqs 6/8/10) applied to the same BEA Benchmark IO matrix family at later vintages. Concept-identical, not concept-substituting. BEA is the canonical and only US source for industry-level technology matrices at this detail.
provenance.vintage_note: Matrix order varies across vintages (71-order 1947-1972, 65-order 1998, 403/171-order 2002+); the aggregate scalar concept is preserved.
provenance.conceptual_continuity_epr_v1: XS2001 measures Sraffa aggregate price/value ratios at observed rates of profit, computed via paper eqs 6/8/10 on the BEA Benchmark IO matrix family. v1.0 verbatim transcribes Tables 1-2 (1947, 1958, 1963, 1967, 1972, 1998); v1.1 extends to the missing benchmark years (1977/1982/1987/1992/2002/2007/2012/2017) by rerunning the identical eigenvalue/left-eigenvector computation on the same BEA-IO matrix family at later vintages — concept-identical, not concept-substituting. BEA Benchmark IO is the only published US source for industry-level technology matrices at the required detail; no alternative agency exists. The scalar aggregate-ratio concept (one (model, year) pair → 9 ratios) is distinct from the cross-sectional p(r) Sraffa price curve concept which lives in sibling series XS2101 (different content_type). Matrix-order discontinuities (71/65/403/171-order across vintages) are documented but do not constitute concept substitution. No proxy substitution forbidden by the No-Proxy rule.

provenance.conceptual_continuity_epr_v1: XS2201 measures the five jointly-fit parameters (G', ⟨r⟩, ⟨w⟩, f, α) of the two-class econophysics income distribution (Dragulescu-Yakovenko exponential bottom + Pareto top), MLE-fit per year on IRS SOI Pub 1304 Tables 1.4 + 1. Paper window 2002-2016 is verbatim Table 1; extension years (2017+) re-fit the same MLE on the same publication at later vintages — NOT growth-rate-spliced from existing parameters (per Anu Framework No Lazy Splices rule, since the five parameters are jointly estimated, not directly observed). IRS SOI Pub 1304 is the only US administrative source supporting the joint MLE; CPS/PSID survey data truncate the Pareto top tail. G' is the bottom-97% Gini, NOT the full-population Gini (Census/CBO/World Bank); α is the top-3% Pareto exponent, NOT the Piketty-Saez top-share statistic; ⟨w⟩ is a regression-derived income temperature, NOT a sample mean. TCJA (2017+) and CARES (2020+) AGI definition revisions create documented methodological discontinuities in extension years but do not constitute concept substitution. No proxy substitution forbidden by the No-Proxy rule.

triage.reason: Weber & Shaikh (2020) Figure 4 is a literature-compilation SCATTER of ~35-40 individual RMB-misalignment estimates whose entire signal is the DISPERSION of the estimates. The chopped series contains only 2 points: the named high (+50%, Coudert & Couharde 2007) and low (-36%, Cheung 2012) that the paper quotes by name in body text. Two isolated dots do not convey the figure's signal (the spread of dozens of estimates) and would misrepresent the study if charted as the figure. Per the no-fabrication rule the project (correctly) declined to chart-digitize the ~35 unnamed scatter dots; the XS2304/XS2305 README explicitly defers full reconstruction to a v1.1 literature-extraction pass. Until that pass populates the full scatter from the 4 cited reviews, this 2-point stub is not publishable. The 2 named endpoints remain documented in the DPR/EPR as the paper's quoted extremes.
